item.title: How I Archive
item.description:
One thing I discovered over the years: I generate a TON of files. A lot of these files are trash and do not need to be referenced in the future. But there are some that I feel iffy about deleting - or even just not really a good idea.

These include:

  1. Past Projects whose architecture I might want to reference
  2. Photos of old documents
  3. Software I purchased which is in danger of just not being available on the internet anymore in the future

For these files, I archive them. And over the few years I started doing so, I optimized it.

item.title: Please use ISO 8601 for your dates in files
item.description:
tl;dr: When you need to state the date, just use YYYY-MM-DD.

ISO 8601 is pretty simple: Date is YYYY-MM-DD and time is HH:MM. Please use it. Benefits include:

  1. Automatic sorting through names. I don’t get how people are NOT annoyed with Jan appearing after Apr in their file lists. Stop. Just use 2026-01-01 and you will always see it before 2026-04-01 unless you sort by other means.
  2. Understandable by anyone. 02-12-2026 can either mean February 12 or December 2. Stop the confusion and use either 2026-12-02 or 2026-02-12.
  3. Automatic versioning. If you add hours and minutes (even as HH-MM), it’s not that hard to think of the next version because you can just use the time you save the file.

Before people tell me that the date is in the metadata, I would really like to say that zipping it or uploading it somewhere can change it. Not to mention a random stray save can ruin your day.

item.title: My Self Hosting Journey after ~18 months
item.description: It’s been around a year and a half since I started self hosting. It all started when I bought a Raspberry Pi for no good reason. I installed a few apps before succumbing to compute limits. At times, it would randomly shut down because it could not get enough power. I cannot even plug an HDD as it would pull too much power. I bought a used Dell Optiplex from a second-hand seller. I think it was a company pull-out which was fine as I got it for just ~1000 PHP. I then upgraded the SSD and the RAM which took ~9000 PHP (this was before the RAMpocalypse and the SSD shortage). And now, for a year, it is going very smoothly.

item.title: Small Scale Database Backups
item.description:
The biggest reason I moved away from the cloud is to have control of my own data. However, that meant knowing how to protect it. Backups are the only way to keep the data truly safe.

item.title: Backups done properly
item.description: I have a lot of VPS (I have a bad habit of collecting them). One of my main fears is losing the data I have. While I could build like 90% of it again from various sources, I would rather not go through the trouble when the inevitable happens. Like you know, accidentally missing the . on rm -r ./. Or a flood. Or just the hard drive deciding it’s done its job and going kapoof. Or getting ransomwared. Or realizing you did a misconfiguration and need to go back. Backups are just a great safety net.
